Hi Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. Looping Ben (pricing) and Jordan (partner ops) — I put together a short worked example and a modeling workbook, attaching both. Key points up front:

- We typically use a 3‑band slab for private offers to balance predictability and upside: Starter (0–50k units), Growth (50k–250k), Scale (250k+).
- Committed discounts are applied to list before channel commissions. Channel netback is calculated on net revenue after committed discount but before any post‑period trueups (so partner sees the committed uplift).
- Retro credits for overage/velocity are processed as post‑period contra invoices — they do not reduce partner commissions already paid; instead we handle partner reconciliation on a monthly/quarterly cadence.

Action items: Ben, can you confirm the % bands and a sample netback table? Jordan, can you confirm partner invoice flow so Alex can share with CloudWave.

Thanks — aiming to get the spreadsheet revision to you by Wed EOD.

Naomi Feldman
Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks Naomi — quick sketch below. I'll attach the same table as an image in the workbook. Numbers are illustrative; final bands we can tune to Dataverse volumes.

Worked example (monthly token-equivalent slabs; prices in $ per 1k token-equivalent units):
- List price per 1k: $0.90
- Starter (0–50k): committed discount 10% -> customer price $0.81; channel commission 12% of customer price -> partner netback = $0.7128 per 1k
- Growth (50k–250k): committed discount 22% -> customer price $0.702; channel commission 10% -> partner netback = $0.6318 per 1k
- Scale (250k+): committed discount 30% -> customer price $0.63; channel commission 8% -> partner netback = $0.5796 per 1k

Notes on overages/retro credits:
- If actual usage exceeds committed bands, we apply velocity uplift credits as a one‑time post‑billing rebate to the customer at the end of the month. Those rebates appear as contra revenue for Redwood; partner reconciliation will include a monthly true‑up file but will not claw back commissions already remitted.

I'll add a short paragraph in the workbook describing tax and GST handling.

Ben Carter
Head of Pricing
Redwood Inference

Alex — quick operational clarification from partner ops:

- Settlement flow: Redwood invoices Dataverse for total customer price (post‑committed discount). Redwood pays CloudWave commission based on the agreed netback % on the invoice amount in the following payroll cycle.
- If a retro rebate is issued to Dataverse, we post a contra invoice and a reconciliation file to CloudWave; CloudWave is credited on their next payout, not retroactively debited.
- For bookkeeping, recommend this language in the SOW addendum: "Channel commissions are calculated on the invoiced customer price after committed discounts; adjustments from post‑billing rebates are reconciled monthly and reflected in subsequent partner settlements."

Connor — can you prep the reconciliation CSV template we use for private offers and share with Alex?

Jordan Blake
Partner Operations
Redwood Inference
